# glassbottles

> glassbottles (https://glassbottles.app) is a free, anonymous "message in a
> bottle" web app. Each day you can write one anonymous message, throw it into
> a digital sea, and a stranger somewhere in the world may find it. In return,
> a stranger's bottle may wash up for you. There are no profiles, no replies,
> no followers, and no feed.

## What it is

- An anonymous message exchange between strangers: one bottle per person per day.
- Messages carry no name, handle, avatar, or history — the finder cannot
  identify or contact the sender.
- Bottles are one-way: a bottle is a moment, not a conversation. There is no
  reply mechanism by design.
- Free to use. Sign-up requires only an email address (or Google sign-in).

## How it works

1. Write something honest — anything you want to say without your name on it.
2. Throw it into the sea. You get one bottle per day; the limit is the point.
3. The next day, another user's bottle may wash ashore for you to read.

## Safety

- Every delivered bottle can be reported. Reported bottles are removed and
  repeat abusers lose access.
- Anonymity protects the writer, never the abuse.

## Key pages

- https://glassbottles.app — landing page: what the app is, how it works, FAQ.
- https://glassbottles.app/sign-up — create a free account.
- https://glassbottles.app/sign-in — sign in.

"message in a bottle app", "anonymous message in a bottle",
"send a message to a stranger online", "digital message in a bottle",
